purpose: The declared-exception ledger read by tools/analysis/creation-audit.mjs. An assertion named here fails as XFAIL instead of FAIL, and the audit still exits non-zero for anything NOT named here. An entry that has stopped being true is reported as STALE and also fails the run, so the ledger cannot rot into a list of excuses. Every entry states what would remove it.
rule: A gap may be declared only when repairing it would mean inventing design the corpus does not contain. A gap may NOT be declared to avoid work.

declared_failures.reason: Nord and Orsimer name the same five skills (Greatweapons, Axes & Maces, Shieldcraft, Survival, Athletics) in RI-CHR02 §1's own table. Their VALUES differ — Nord 25/20/15/10/10, Orsimer 20/25/20/10/5 — so the two races do not start with the same numbers, and CHR02-M1-distinct-skill-profiles (asserted hard, 10/10) covers that. Changing either row to make the ID sets differ would be inventing a skill assignment the corpus did not write.
declared_failures.removed_by: RI-CHR02's owner either restating method 1 as 'no two identical skill PROFILES', or changing one cell of the Nord or Orsimer row.
declared_failures.impact: None on play. A Nord and an Orsimer are still distinguishable at creation by their attribute deltas (0/4 shared cells), their skill values, their abilities and eight of twelve reaction-matrix cells.

declared_content_gaps.what: RI-PRG03 ships 19 skills including Polearms, but no race in RI-CHR02 §1 and no named class in RI-CHR01 §4 raises Polearms above baseline. The named-class route reaches 18 of 19.
declared_content_gaps.shipped: The corpus tables verbatim. Polearms IS reachable above baseline via route B (custom) and is weighted in five questionnaire answers (route C), so no build is locked out of it, and the audit asserts 19/19 across the 15 class options RI-CHR01 method 2 counts.
declared_content_gaps.removed_by: one named class gaining Polearms as a primary or secondary — a one-cell change RI-CHR01's owner must make, not this builder.

declared_content_gaps.what: The dres-raid-party is specified as 4-6 INFANTRY + 1 CASTER + 2 net-throwers. It ships with six members and no CASTER, because W1-07 does not own a caster statblock and inventing one would be inventing frame data.
declared_content_gaps.removed_by: W1-12 (enemy AI) or a magic piece shipping a caster statblock with real frame data; the encounter then names it.

declared_content_gaps.judged_by: RI-CHR02 method 5 (§4c minimums: 1,500 greeting lines, 90 race-filtered topics, 60 slavery lines)
declared_content_gaps.what: W1-07 owns the reaction MATRIX and every term downstream of it. It does not own the dialogue corpus those terms key into; that is W1-11..W1-13. The five channels are specified in race-reactions.json and the greeting key is implemented (playerRaceClass), but the line volume is not shipped by this piece.
declared_content_gaps.removed_by: the dialogue pieces writing against the shipped key.

declared_content_gaps.judged_by: RI-CHR02 method 4 (population shares within +/-4 points of §2)
declared_content_gaps.what: Five NPC records exist in game/data/npcs/** in wave 1. All five carry a reaction_group and the audit asserts that hard; the POPULATION SHARE half of method 4 is not assertable until the settlement rosters exist.
declared_content_gaps.removed_by: W1-04 (settlements) and W1-11..13 (dialogue) populating the eight settlements; the audit's npcs section then asserts shares as well as coverage.

declared_corpus_discrepancies.reason: PRE-EMPTIVE, currently passing at the restated bar. RI-CHR02 §4b prints 'Round-trip vs Saxhleel' as -30% (Imperial) and -44% (Dunmer) without giving the definition, and no reading of 'round trip' reproduces BOTH numbers from the item's own buy/sell multipliers. The audit prints four candidate readings for both races and asserts the claim the item does make unambiguously: a Dunmer loses at least two fifths of a round trip against a Saxhleel. Measured: -49.5% on the sell/buy-ratio reading.
declared_corpus_discrepancies.removed_by: RI-CHR02's owner stating the formula behind that column.
declared_corpus_discrepancies.impact: The shipped surcharge is HARSHER than the item's printed column, not softer, so no bar is being dodged.
